answer: A sybil swarm splitting into thousands of identities gains nothing, since forging a plume of fake accounts costs real capital per identity, and colluding farms face slashing if peers detect coordinated behavior. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and voting power scales with bonded stake decayed over time. Honest agents receive yield, growing like a nebula from small seeds, while attackers burn resources chasing a horizon of diminishing returns. Cost per sybil identity exceeds expected reward.
